title: Rush DevKit stack preset
description: A preset packages what the kit needs to know about one stack: how detect-stack.sh recognises it, the commands used to verify work, the prose conventions worth seeding into CLAUDE.md/constitution.md, starter fitness functions, config overrides, and (for greenfield projects) the official scaffold command. rush-init consumes a preset for an existing project (matching it against the detected stack); rush-new consumes it to bootstrap a new project from scratch via `scaffold`.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, matched against detect-stack.sh's preset_suggestion field and used as the preset's filename (<id>.json). Never rename once published — projects may reference it.

name.description: Short human-readable name shown to the user when rush-init proposes this preset, e.g. 'NestJS + Prisma'.

description.description: One dense sentence: what stack this covers and what kind of project it fits. Shown alongside `name` when a user is choosing between presets.

match.description: Deterministic signals detect-stack.sh uses to recognise this stack in an existing repository. Every listed signal is a plain string match against files already on disk — never a guess, never something requiring network access.

dependencies.description: Package names that, if present in the project's manifest (package.json dependencies/devDependencies, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, etc.), count as a signal for this preset. Order does not matter; matching is existence-based, not version-based.

files.description: Relative file paths or globs whose presence signals this stack (e.g. 'nest-cli.json', 'next.config.js', 'alembic.ini').

lockfiles.description: Lockfile names that, combined with the other signals, confirm the package manager / ecosystem in use (e.g. 'package-lock.json', 'pnpm-lock.yaml', 'poetry.lock').

commands.description: Real, ecosystem-correct CLI invocations this preset seeds into config.json → commands when adopted. Any field left out means that command is not applicable or not standardised enough for this stack to assume; rush-init leaves it null rather than guessing.

test.description: Command that runs the test suite for this stack.

lint.description: Command that runs static lint checks for this stack.

build.description: Command that builds/compiles the project for this stack.

format.description: Command that auto-formats code for this stack.

typecheck.description: Command that runs static type checking for this stack, where the ecosystem has one as a distinct step.

conventions.description: Prose rules that seed CLAUDE.md and constitution.md for a project adopting this preset. Every entry must be an EARNED rule: traceable to a real constraint of the stack (a footgun the framework has, a failure mode the ecosystem is known for, a structural property that must hold for the framework's own guarantees to hold) — never a bare style preference. `reason` is mandatory precisely so a human reviewing the preset can reject rules that turn out to be taste dressed up as principle.

rule.description: The rule itself, stated as a single imperative sentence suitable for pasting into CLAUDE.md or constitution.md.

reason.description: Why this rule is earned: the concrete constraint, failure mode, or framework guarantee it protects. This is what a reviewer checks before accepting the rule into a real project.

severity.description: 'must' = binding constitution-level rule, violating it blocks a gate. 'should' = strong default, worth a comment in review but not an automatic block.

structure.description: Where this stack conventionally places code, tests and migrations, relative to the project root. Used to seed architecture.md and to give rush-explorer a starting point instead of a blind search.

code.description: Relative path where application source code lives, e.g. 'src/'.

tests.description: Relative path where tests live, e.g. 'test/' or 'tests/'.

migrations.description: Relative path where database schema migrations live, if this stack has migrations. Omit for stacks without a migration concept.

fitness_functions.description: Starter executable checks seeded into .rush/memory/fitness/ for a project adopting this preset, run by fitness.sh. Each one encodes a real architectural constraint of the stack, not an arbitrary style preference — the same 'earned rule' bar as `conventions`.

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier for the check, used as the seeded script's filename stem (<name>.sh).

description.description: One sentence: what architectural constraint this enforces and why it matters for this stack. Becomes the '# description:' header fitness.sh reads.

scope.description: 'all' to run against the whole project every time, or a feature id pattern to scope it to specific features. Becomes the '# scope:' header fitness.sh reads.

script.description: The full body of the fitness function script (POSIX-portable bash, no GNU-only flags, no jq — see docs/internals/script-interfaces.md), written out verbatim so rush-init can create it as-is. Must exit 0 when the constraint holds and a non-zero exit with an explanatory message when it does not.

config_overrides.description: Partial config.json merged over config.default.json when this preset is adopted (e.g. stack-appropriate autonomy defaults, sensitive_paths seeded from files.match). Must be a subset of config.schema.json's shape; rush-init validates the merged result before writing config.json.

scaffold.description: For greenfield use via rush-new: the official generator command(s) for this stack, plus anything that must run right after scaffolding to leave the project in a state the rest of the kit can work with. Omit entirely for a preset meant only to match existing projects.

commands.description: Ordered list of shell commands that create a new project of this stack, using each ecosystem's own official generator (e.g. `npx @nestjs/cli new .`, `npx create-next-app@latest .`). rush-new runs these in order and stops on the first non-zero exit.

post_scaffold.description: Ordered list of shell commands run after `commands` succeed, to adapt the generator's default output to the kit's expectations (e.g. installing a test runner the generator does not include by default, wiring an ORM). Kept minimal and non-destructive — this is finishing the official scaffold, not replacing it.

contract_style.description: The interface contract style validate-contracts.sh should expect for features built on this stack: 'rest-openapi' for HTTP APIs described with OpenAPI, 'graphql' for a GraphQL schema, 'events' for AsyncAPI/event-driven contracts. Determines which contract files rush-contracts generates by default.
